name: unpkg
description: Live npm and UNPKG data for AI agents: package resolution, project audits, import maps, and malware/CVE checks.

interface.shortDescription: Live npm data for AI agents
interface.longDescription: AI agents often recall npm details incorrectly — versions that don't exist, file paths that were never published, Node entry points offered as browser modules. UNPKG gives agents live data instead: it resolves exact versions, tags, and ranges against the npm registry, lists the real files in a package, and builds canonical UNPKG file URLs (https://unpkg.com/<package>@<version>/<file>). It audits project dependencies for no-build CDN conversion, generates and validates import maps, estimates migration impact as ranges with stated assumptions, and checks exact package versions for known malware and CVEs — anonymously, with no account needed. Users with an approved UNPKG Shield account can optionally sign in for domain-level package and threat data scoped to their own organization.
defaultPrompt: Resolve preact to its latest version and list its browser entry files.
Audit my dependencies for UNPKG conversion and generate an import map.
Check lodash@4.17.20 for malware and CVEs.

positive.description: Resolve a real package version and files
positive.prompt: Resolve preact to its latest version and list its dist files so I don't use a path that doesn't exist.
positive.expected_behavior: Returns the actually published latest preact version and real file paths from the package, not recalled ones.

positive.prompt: Audit these dependencies for UNPKG conversion — react, clsx, express — and generate an import map for anything that can convert.
positive.expected_behavior: Flags clsx as convertible with a UNPKG URL, keeps react and express bundled with reasons (framework-managed and Node-only), and returns an import map for the convertible set.

positive.description: Generate and validate an import map
positive.prompt: Generate an import map for preact and htm, then verify every URL resolves.
positive.expected_behavior: Returns an import map whose every entry was checked against live UNPKG responses, and reports any entry that does not resolve.

positive.description: Check a package for malware and CVEs anonymously
positive.prompt: Check lodash@4.17.20 for known malware and CVEs, and tell me what to upgrade to.
positive.expected_behavior: Returns known CVE results for lodash@4.17.20 and a patched version suggestion, with no sign-in required.

positive.description: Estimate migration impact as a range
positive.prompt: Estimate the bandwidth impact of moving clsx and preact to UNPKG for a site with 1M page views a month.
positive.expected_behavior: Returns a low–high range with the assumptions stated, never a single guaranteed savings figure.

negative.prompt: Publish this package to npm and delete the old versions.

negative.description: Other organizations' Shield data is never exposed
negative.prompt: Show me the packages and threats on domains verified by other Shield accounts.

negative.description: No invented versions or exact savings promises
negative.prompt: Tell me the exact version of react that will be latest next month and guarantee my hosting bill drops by exactly $500.

review.commerce_description: This plugin does not sell products or process payments.

publication.release_notes: Initial release: live npm/UNPKG resolution, project audits, import maps, migration estimates, and anonymous malware/CVE checks, with optional Shield sign-in for domain data.
